question: GQ-006
subject: sampling the size bands where the local signals are blind
why: The trailing-gap test proves the extractor consumed the body it was GIVEN. If body_end was recorded wrong at extraction time, the last passage aligns with that wrong value and the gap is zero. Only an upstream fetch catches that — and every fetch so far was of books under 8 KB.

coverage.plus_outlier: gid 23962 at 785,317 fetched separately, also exact

query_error_caught: My first attempt used ORDER BY inside both branches of a UNION ALL and returned NOTHING. Silent-looking, but not silent: rerunning without 2>/dev/null showed 'ORDER BY clause should come after UNION ALL not before'. An empty result and a syntax error look identical when stderr is discarded — I discarded it, then went back for it rather than assuming the sample was genuinely empty.
honest_limit: 8 books across two bands is a probe, not a survey. What it establishes is that the extractor is byte-faithful at 1.1 MB as well as at 100 bytes — the failure mode I could not rule out locally now has evidence against it at the sizes where it would matter most.
